title: Min-Max Subarray Sum Stack
description:
Design a stack `MinMaxSubarrayStack` of signed integers that supports `push`, `pop`, `top`, and querying BOTH the **minimum** and **maximum sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray** currently in the stack (ordered from bottom to top), all in **`O(1)` time** per operation.

Implement the `MinMaxSubarrayStack` class:
- `MinMaxSubarrayStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the top of the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `long getMinSubarraySum()` returns the minimum sum over all non-empty contiguous segments of elements currently in the stack.
- `long getMaxSubarraySum()` returns the maximum sum over all non-empty contiguous segments of elements currently in the stack.
constraints: Methods pop, top, getMinSubarraySum, and getMaxSubarraySum are always called on non-empty stacks.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Because pushing only appends at the top of the stack, Kadane's recurrence naturally augments each stack frame in O(1) time.

Store `(val, curMinEnding, bestMin, curMaxEnding, bestMax)` per stack frame: pushing updates both Kadane states from the previous top, and popping automatically restores the exact prior states in O(1).

examples.explanation: Stack [3, -5, -2]: min subarray is [-5, -2] (-7) and max subarray is [3] (3). Pushing 10 raises max subarray to [10] (10); popping 10 restores max to 3.
All-negative stack [-4, -1, -3]: min subarray is the whole stack (-8) and max subarray is [-1] (-1).
Single element 7 has min subarray sum 7 and max subarray sum 7.
